calls.head: Shots should fly both ways
calls.body: Minnesota plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Nashville. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 85.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Minnesota 3rd (85.1), Nashville 7th (84.0)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 87.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 85.1 and a league average of 81.9.

calls.head: Sheltered against exposed
calls.body: On preventing dangerous shots, Minnesota is one of the league’s best and Nashville is around the middle of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Wild prevent dangerous shots better than the Predators do.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot allowed was, Minnesota had 3.8% a shot and Nashville 5.6% a shot. Coming in, Minnesota was at 6.0% a shot and Nashville at 6.4% a shot.
calls.usual: MIN 6.0% a shot · NSH 6.4% a shot
calls.tonight: MIN 3.8% a shot · NSH 5.6% a shot
calls.beyond: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (48% for Nashville), and it went Minnesota’s way.

MIN.head: We had this close to even (52% for Minnesota), and Minnesota came through.

surprises.head: Minnesota leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Minnesota’s bottom-six forwards played 45% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Minnesota dominated the shot count
surprises.body: Minnesota took 62% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). These two usually split the shots about evenly. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Wild beat the Predators
paras: Nick Foligno opened the scoring midway through the first. Blake Coleman scored the winner late in the first.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Wild win about four in five. By our Swing measure, Kirill Kaprizov had the best night of anyone.

items.text: Both of the preview’s calls held.
